facts.statement: Protoplatyrhina bourdoni is a newly described species (sp. nov).
The species Protoplatyrhina bourdoni was described by Goode.
Protoplatyrhina bourdoni lived during the Cretaceous period.
The type locality of Protoplatyrhina bourdoni is the Point Lookout Sandstone in New Mexico, United States.
Protoplatyrhina bourdoni was found in the United States, specifically New Mexico.
The genus Protoplatyrhina belongs to the parent group Rhinobatoidei.
Protoplatyrhina is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossils of the genus Protoplatyrhina are recorded from the Turonian to Maastrichtian, about 93.9 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A study reexamining Protoplatyrhina was published in The Anatomical Record in 2026 by Benjamin Spencer Goode.
Protoplatyrhina bourdoni sp. nov. was erected for teeth recovered from the Hosta Tongue of the Point Lookout Sandstone in New Mexico, USA.
The family Protoplatyrhinidae fam. nov. was created to include Protoplatyrhina and related taxa.
Researchers consider the phylogenetic position of Protoplatyrhina to be contested.
The presence of a lingual crown uvula on Protoplatyrhina teeth is variable, being less pronounced than in most Protoplatyrhina renae teeth.
